sources.entry: TypeCue - Types a prepared script into any app, one hotkey press per line, as real keystrokes at a human pace, for demo recordings and live presentations.

summary.one_liner: TypeCue is a macOS menu bar app that types a prepared script into any focused field, one block per global hotkey press, as real keystrokes at a human pace.
summary.what_it_does: TypeCue stores a demo or presentation script as ordered text blocks and types the next block into whichever field has focus each time a global hotkey (default Ctrl+Option+X) is pressed. It sends system-level keystrokes with human-like pacing, and the README claims identical output on every take. Inline markers control pauses ([0.5], [2]), typing speed ([speed:40]), and Return ([enter]). Line breaks inside a block are typed as Shift+Return by default. A floating teleprompter panel shows each block's state (typed, typing, next, upcoming) without taking focus. Scripts are plain JSON that AI agents can edit, and the app is controlled through typecue:// URL commands and a state.json mirror.
use_cases: recording demo videos with scripted typing
live presentations where typing must be controlled
tutorial and webinar typing on screen
letting an AI agent author typing scripts
how_to_run: Or download the latest release, drag TypeCue to Applications, and grant Accessibility permission
notable: Types real system keystrokes, with a Unicode fallback for characters not on the active layout
Inline pacing markers for pauses, per-character speed, and Return
Scripts are plain JSON, with a typecue:// command scheme and state.json mirror for automation
Ships an agent skill file for AI tools to author and drive scripts
Floating teleprompter panel that does not steal focus
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ to run and Xcode 16.4+ to build
Password and secure fields block synthetic typing system-wide, a macOS rule; TypeCue shows a warning instead of typing
UI tests need an interactive GUI session
